A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViaSHAP study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–O support reliable comparison; the shorter v2 reflects layout changes rather than missing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on 25 tabular datasets and CIFAR-10, including predictive performance, explanation accuracy, ablations and computational timings.

after.justification: v2 retains the original tabular and CIFAR-10 experiments, ablations and timing results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same prediction procedure, dual training objective and model components. The KAN, MLP and image implementations, including the relaxed variant in Appendix G, are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 25 tabular datasets listed in Table 19 and CIFAR-10 image classification in Appendix F. No evaluated task, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain XGBoost, Random Forests and TabNet in Table 1, the KAN control in Table 10, FastSHAP in Tables 5 and 16, and KernelSHAP in the explanation and timing evaluations.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, model configurations and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Both retain the tabular defaults of beta = 10 and 32 sampled coalitions, along with the same image-training settings and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Appendices G–J retain the same analyses of the relaxed prediction baseline, marginal expectations, Shapley loss, beta, coalition counts, link functions, efficiency constraints and training losses. The image explanation examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same five-seed or five-run reporting, means and standard deviations, confidence intervals in Tables 4–5, and Friedman, Nemenyi and Wilcoxon significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: The result entries in Tables 1–18 and the corresponding plots and qualitative examples are unchanged. No numerical scores, timings, rankings or reported empirical findings are added, removed or revised.

T1.justification: The definitions, Lemmas 3.1–3.3, Theorem 3.4 and proofs in Appendices A–C remain unchanged. Equation (10) adds a missing class subscript j inside the prediction-loss term, aligning notation with the existing per-class formulation without revising the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: predicting through learned Shapley values, exploring KAN and neural-network implementations, competitive tabular prediction and more accurate explanations than FastSHAP.

C2.justification: The new Impact Statement explains that Shapley-accurate explanations may lack causal or domain-relevant reasoning, encourage misplaced trust, or facilitate reverse-engineering and adversarial misuse. These qualifications supplement the unchanged technical limitations in Appendix M.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, code-access information, hardware specifications and dataset split details are retained. Moving the computational-cost figure adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 removes the duplicate 2020 preprint entry for Covert et al.'s Explaining by Removing and redirects its citation to the already-listed 2021 journal version. This represents the same cited work; the substantive research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Impact Statement after the acknowledgements, adds an author affiliation, and makes limited spelling, punctuation, phrasing and notation corrections. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 20 is resized and moved from a separate page in v1 onto the computational-cost discussion page in v2. The first page and references also reflow, while figure contents, captions and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new Impact Statement usefully distinguishes accurate Shapley attribution from causal explanation and addresses misplaced trust and misuse, improving the interpretation of the retained findings. Small editorial corrections and placing Figure 20 beside its discussion improve clarity. The methodological and empirical evidence remains unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
